notes: Downloads are lossless now. Every converter opens on FLAC (lossless) \u2014 the same audio with nothing thrown away, about a fifth of a WAV’s size \u2014 with WAV (also lossless) next and MP3 last for when space matters more. Pick MP3 at any time from the same format menu, on the album picker, the single-song converter and the YouTube one

The FLAC encoder no longer freezes the app. It used to run the whole track in one pass on the main thread, which is why a lossless conversion locked everything up; it now hands the screen back every couple of seconds of audio and reports progress, and the file it writes is byte-for-byte the one it always wrote

Artists are comma-separated everywhere. The file-name cleaner stripped commas, so a converted "Diljit Dosanjh, Sia" became "Diljit Dosanjh Sia" and the library filed that as ONE artist. Commas survive now, so the file name, the saved tag and the library row all read "Diljit Dosanjh, Sia" \u2014 and a credit written "A & B", "A x B" or "A feat. B" is normalized to "A, B" on the way in, on imports too
Every credited artist is used, not just the first. A Spotify track whose credits are Diljit Dosanjh, Sia and David Guetta came out as "Diljit Dosanjh" only; the whole credit list is read now

Rename an album and its artist in one go. The Rename button in Manage albums asks for the album name AND the artist printed under it. If the album already shares one artist the songs are renamed with it; a mixed-artist album keeps each song’s own artist

The record player opens the album properly. In Albums, tapping it used to end in a toast when the album card had not been opened yet \u2014 its song rows are only built when the card is expanded, and a re-render rebuilds the cards closed. It now opens the card itself, scrolls to the playing song and highlights it, with no toast anywhere in that path
